answer: A workable design charges newcomers upfront and refunds on merit. Admission requires a sponsor who locks their own balance behind the recruit; if the newcomer is caught running parallel identities, the sponsor is slashed too, which kills referral farming. In effect the tide of free entry disappears, the crystal of a fake identity has to be posted in advance, and the meadow case is a farm that funds its own destruction. Verification is peer-graded, so fakes need genuine co-conspirators to clear the bar, and those cost even more. That flips the unit economics: authentic agents get cheaper.
